messages:
alice: Quick heads-up — scheduling a 2h maintenance window on Sunday for the runtime kernel + quantization micro-upgrade. Target window: Sun 2025-04-06 02:00–04:00 UTC. This is to fix a rare OOM in long-chat sessions and enable a faster int8 path. Need statuspage copy and short customer email draft.

bob: +1. Do we have canary results? deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded on 3/30, 10/10 requests passed, observed 7% median latency improvement. No regressions in our smoke evals.

carol: Flag: Dedicated customers on pinned infra might need manual pin changes if we force an image rollout. Suggest we offer a no-rollback window option for those on reserved capacity.

mike: From CS: please include clear guidance about potential short bursts of 5–10m elevated error rates and how to reach on-call. Also include timezone conversions for PST/CET/APAC.

alice: Agreed. Draft statuspage copy below — please sanity-check.

alice: STATUSPAGE DRAFT:
- Summary: Scheduled maintenance to upgrade inference runtime kernel to improve memory handling and latency for long sessions.
- Start: Sun Apr 6, 2025 02:00 UTC (Sun Apr 5 19:00 PDT / Sun Apr 6 03:00 CEST)
- Duration: up to 2 hours
- Impact: Short, rolling restarts of serving nodes. Customers may experience brief (5–10m) elevated error rates or increased latency as capacity cycles. No data loss expected.
- Mitigation: Canary validated; rollback steps ready; we will monitor and pause if error rates exceed 1% above baseline for >15m.
- Contact: status.redwood.com and support@redwood.ai for urgent issues.

support-lead: Nice. Add line about Dedicated customers: "If you are on Redwood Dedicated and have pinning configured, contact support to opt into the new runtime or request a coordinated upgrade."

alice: Updated. Now an email/snippet for customers (short):

alice: EMAIL DRAFT:
Subject: Planned maintenance — inference runtime upgrade (Apr 6, 02:00 UTC)
Hello —
We will be performing a scheduled upgrade to our inference runtime on Apr 6, 02:00 UTC to improve stability and reduce memory errors for long-chat workloads. The window may cause short, rolling restarts of serving nodes and brief elevated errors for up to 10 minutes at a time.
If you use Redwood Dedicated with version pinning, please contact support to schedule a coordinated upgrade.
If you experience production impact, contact support@redwood.ai or open a ticket and we will prioritize remediation.
Thanks — Redwood Inference Ops

bob: Suggest adding a one-line rollback note: "If we detect regressions, we will roll back within the window and follow up with post-mortem notes."

alice: Added. Now we need a short statuspage incident message for ops to paste in if we hit >1% errors.

carol: PUT THIS AS IRC SNIPPET:
We are pausing the maintenance and rolling back the runtime upgrade due to elevated error rates above threshold. Engineers are reverting images and validating traffic. Estimated restoration in 15–30m.

mike: Also add a canned Slack reply for CS: "We're aware and monitoring. We're rolling back if errors persist; opening a high-priority ticket for your org."

deploy-bot: Canary: all checks green, but note: one cluster showed degraded KV cache warm-up at scale; trending only under synthetic long-history tests. Recommend enabling "graceful-warmup" flag during rollout.

alice: Good catch. We'll include "graceful-warmup" in the rollout plan and call it out in the ops runbook.

support-lead: Action items: 1) Post statuspage scheduled maintenance with copy above — target publish 24h before window. 2) Send customer email to active customers in next 18h. 3) Notify Dedicated customers via CS with opt-in line. 4) Ops: include rollback play and graceful-warmup flag in runbook. 5) On-call: set 15m alert threshold for error-rate spikes.

alice: I'll publish the statuspage draft and email to the comms repo in 20m. Please review there and ping me with edits. @mike please coordinate Dedicated customer outreach. :thumbsup:

mike: On it. I'll prepare a short list of pinned accounts and draft personalized opt-in asks.

carol: I'll update the rollout config and put the graceful-warmup flag in the canary job.

bob: Ops will bake the quick rollback script and test locally.

alice: Thanks team — closing thread.
